posts.title: Drive a case interview by proposing your next step after every answer instead of waiting to be told

posts.title: Case interview maths is simple arithmetic done out loud, so state your approach, round smartly and sanity-check
posts.description: The arithmetic is simple; doing it out loud under pressure is not. Approach first, round smartly, sanity-check everything.

What is 15% of 480? 2. Fixed costs $3M, price $25, variable cost $10. Breakeven volume? 3. Cost $80, price $100. Which is true? Try it now

posts.title: How can the client make more profit? Use the profitability framework to find whether revenue or costs moved

A national bank's mortgage applications are down 20% this year. Why? 2. A ski resort's profits fell 40% after two warm winters. 3. A cinema chain's attendance is still 25% below pre-pandemic levels.

posts.title: Stage 1 of a case: listen closely and write the client's goal at the top of your page
posts.description: Everything later links back to the goal you write down now. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Listen and note Don’t fake understanding Draw early insights Practise the moment The interviewer has just finished reading the prompt to you. What do you say first? Mid-prompt, the interviewer says "the client’s contribution has fallen" and you’re not sure what they mean by contribution. You hear: "volumes are stable but revenue is down

posts.title: Stage 2 of a case: recap the client, the problem and the goal in one or two sentences
posts.description: Shows you listened, and checks you are solving the right problem. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Recap the key points only Practise the moment The prompt was: a UK gym chain, revenue up 5%, profit halved, the CEO wants it fixed within a year. Give your recap.

posts.title: Stage 3 of a case: ask at most three clarifying questions, and only ones that change your structure
posts.description: The right question can split the whole case in two before you draw anything. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Pick the questions that matter Ask to build, not to stall Ask for thinking time Practise the moment You’ve recapped and asked your clarifying questions. You need time to think. A profitability case. Which single question splits the case in two? The prompt says the client "wants to grow" but gives no number. Ask about the goal. You don’t

posts.title: Stage 4 of a case: lay out a structure tailored to the client and say where you would start
posts.description: Interviewers weigh it heavily. Your structure is your plan for the whole case. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Draw it Check it is MECE Present it top-down Practise the moment You’ve drawn a three-bucket structure for a market entry case. Present it. You finish presenting your structure. What do you NOT say?

posts.title: Stage 5 of a case: lead by proposing the next step and the data you need after every answer
posts.description: Interviewers score whether you drive. Waiting to be told what to do loses candidate-led cases. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Propose, don’t wait Summarise at the turns Practise the moment You’ve just answered a question about costs. Keep driving the case. You’ve covered two of your three buckets. Summarise and steer.

posts.title: Stage 6 of a case: take a moment with each chart and give insights, not a description
posts.description: Exhibits test whether you can find what matters, and many cases turn on them. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Take a moment Insights, not description If stuck or wrong Practise the moment The interviewer hands you a dense chart. You’ve read the chart. Start your answer. You realise your reading of the chart was wrong.

posts.title: Stage 7 of a case: agree your approach before the numbers, calculate out loud and sanity-check
posts.description: Numbers turn opinions into evidence. Errors under pressure are the most common confidence killer. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Approach before arithmetic Always sanity-check Market sizing extras Practise the moment You’re asked to estimate the profit impact of a new product line. What do you say before any numbers? You’ve calculated $100M of revenue from 2M units at $50. Finish the calculation properly. A market sizing question: "How many dentists are there in

posts.title: Stage 8 of a case: brainstorm in buckets and add one real-world example
posts.description: Even open questions are structuring questions in disguise. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Structure even here Add one real example Practise the moment "What could the client do to retain customers?" Open your answer. Add a real-world example to a retention idea.

posts.title: Stage 9 of a case: give the answer first, with reasons, risks and next steps, in about 60 seconds
posts.description: The last 60 seconds are what the interviewer remembers and writes up. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Answer first Park what you didn’t cover Practise the moment The interviewer says: "The CEO walks in. What do you tell her?" You never got to the cost side of your structure. Where does it go?

posts.title: Throughout a case: stay calm, link every answer to the goal and treat it as a conversation
posts.description: You are being judged on how you come across in every minute, not just the answers. What to do, what to say, and the mistake to avoid.
posts.k: stages communication Why it matters The common mistake What to do, and what to say Presence Good habits Link everything back Practise the moment You’ve just given an answer about falling sales in one region. Add a habit that separates strong candidates. The interviewer mentions the new plant will cost $150M to build. What do you ask about?
